_comment: The scheduled tournament roster (Story 5.3, FR-20).
Shape is FR-20's arithmetic, not taste: 3 Deployments + 3 Baseline Bots = 6 Agents,
round-robin = 15 pairings per seed, over 30 seeds, each played from BOTH sides
(Story 7.1, AD-12) = 900 Matches, of which each Deployment plays 300.
Story 7.1 doubled those numbers from 450 / 150 and that is deliberate: a pairing
played from one side only cannot tell a side advantage in the Environment apart from
a skill difference, which is the one thing the leaderboard exists to report. The
price is that ~4,500 calls per Deployment becomes ~9,000, so a run spans about nine
weekday segments against the 1,000-RPD ceiling instead of 4.5. The runner is
resumable (AD-9), so the run converges; it just takes longer.
`seedCount` is NOT halved to buy that time back. 15 seeds would leave every pairing
sitting exactly on the 30-Match rating floor, where one missing log makes the pairing
permanently provisional.
One RANKED Deployment per provider. Two would contend for a single daily quota,
and `validateTournamentConfig` warns about exactly that; `main.ts` prints the
warning to stderr rather than swallowing it.
Models are the highest-RPD row in each provider's block of
`packages/providers/src/free-tier.config.json`. Read that file before editing a
model name here: an endpoint absent from its allowlist fails configuration
validation (INV-8), and Google bakes the model into the URL path, so each Google
model is its own allowlist entry.
`seedBase` MUST NOT change between segments of a running tournament. The plan is a
pure function of this config, so editing it re-plans 900 different matchIds and the
resume would never converge -- every segment would start from zero forever.
`apiKeyEnv` names an environment variable. It is never a key, and there is no field
here that could hold one. In CI these names are bound from Actions secrets by
`.github/workflows/tournament.yml`.
